independentFindings.finding: Shared safe shape functions accept an already valid full reference and compare family and exact table size only. They do not establish raw pointer readability, required slots, provider lifetime or BuildSet admission. Editor gateway directly uses shared V8 shape; App uses independent local validate_v8_api, correcting the old relationship while retaining historical JSON.

Null optional Host pointer returns without dereference; nonnull alignment is checked before shared borrow. Readability/initialization/full table validity and borrow lifetime come from the unsafe contract and live synchronous caller. One authorized ordinary SAFETY line states those premises; it claims no dangling/mapping detection.

Metadata guards do not prove payload readability. Unsafe caller owns a unique allocation and keeps matching provider/session/callback alive; decode returns owned data and terminates borrow before release. Releaser Copy does not duplicate allocation ownership or retain library. Canonical empty has no release callback.

Decode/validator/release callback run outside acceptance gate; final acceptance holds mutex and rechecks fuse after release. First rejection fuses once; later in-flight value is rejected. Metrics across atomics are not a transactional snapshot.

A ProtocolViolation error value does not itself update RuntimeForeignOutputState. App/Editor conversions only map the error. The specific HST-001 empty-cleanup branch returns the diagnostic protocol error without reject; existing Runtime status producer bound is not generalized to all unsafe ABI providers.

Fixed add(1) on a u8 array is not a language-level guarantee of misalignment; assert_ne occurs before unsafe validator call. This remains an open fixture intent/portability TODO without claimed executed failure.
